description.en-US:
caracole keeps a copy of your caracole library on the phone and runs caracole
there, so it works with the computer off.

* Your library, offline: the library page, every sheet with all its tools
  (key, capo, chord diagrams, harmony, pinyin, strum), kept versions,
  harmonica tabs and songbooks.
* Search and fetch from the phone: the computer's site indexes come with a
  sync, so the phone's search finds songs on the sites offline.
* Sync with your computer: the two libraries each take what the other
  changed; where both changed a song, you pick which to keep.
* Guitar Pro on the phone: a file drawn as score and tab and played.
* Share to caracole: share a song from a music app to find it or fetch it.
* Chords from audio: give it a song's audio file and it works out the
  chords and the beats on the phone, under the lyrics it finds, with no
  computer. It needs Android 13, an arm64 phone and 6 GB of memory, and
  downloads its models once, at a tap (about 55 MB, from caracole's GitHub
  release and the chord model's authors' repository).
* A sheet from a YouTube video: paste or share a video and the phone takes
  its audio with its own yt-dlp and makes the song's sheet from it. It also
  does so by itself, on Wi-Fi, for a song no sheet site has (a setting turns
  that off). Taking audio from YouTube goes against YouTube's terms. It needs
  the chord models and an arm64 phone.

It needs a computer running caracole serve to sync from:
https://github.com/Danielhp95/caracole
